_doc: OPS-SHARED-WORKTREE-STATE-REGISTRY-W1 — the SoT for every resource shared ACROSS worktrees on a developer machine. Worktrees isolate the git INDEX and nothing else: $GIT_COMMON_DIR/hooks/*, ~/.crypto-quant-signal/performance.db, the $GIT_COMMON_DIR ledgers and shared deploy checkouts are all common to every checkout. CLAUDE.md's own law — 'a shared primitive gets a CONSUMER REGISTRY, not just drift detection; detection is strictly weaker than enumeration' — was applied to host monitoring artefacts and never to developer-machine state, which is why the 4th writer to pre-push broke every session on 2026-08-01. Read by scripts/check-shared-state.mjs. Missing or unparseable ⇒ SHARED_STATE_VERDICT=INDETERMINATE, exit 3 — never a pass.
_consumers_policy: consumers[] is ENUMERATED, never a count. Where the consumer set is genuinely dynamic (every live worktree governed by a shared hook), the row carries `consumers_derived_from` — the exact command that enumerates it — and check-shared-state.mjs PRINTS the enumeration at runtime. Freezing 75 worktree paths into a committed file would be stale within the hour; a hand-maintained COUNT is forbidden outright (this repo has already had '3 send paths'→8 and '6th consumer'→12 drift unnoticed).
_sha256_policy: ONE canonical sha256 per fact, and for most rows here that hash lives somewhere else already. Repo-tracked scripts are integrity-checked by git itself. The two ops/ artefacts below carry `inventory_ref` because ops/monitoring/monitoring-inventory.json already records their canonical sha256 and reconciles it daily — recording it a second time would be a second thing that can drift, which is the exact failure mode the monitoring-inventory arc codified. The generated hooks are machine-local and rewritten by every install, so a hash of them is meaningless by construction. A null sha256 here always carries its reason.
_skip_ledger_stale_threshold_reason: The skip ledger records a guard that ran nowhere. With 69 of 75 checkouts missing at least one gate script on 2026-08-02, a normal week legitimately produces dozens of rows, so a low threshold would fire constantly and teach the operator to ignore it. 200 flags a genuinely persistent unguarded population without crying wolf during the reclamation backlog. Re-tune when OPS-WORKTREE-RECLAIM-W{NEXT} lands and the population drops.

resources.invariant: Exactly one pre-push hook governs EVERY checkout. It is composable (append/replace by block name, never truncate a sibling) and block order is canonical, so the file is a function of which blocks are installed and not of installer sequence.
resources._sha256_reason: Machine-local and regenerated by every installer run; a recorded hash would drift on the first legitimate install. Integrity comes from the emitter (scripts/lib/hook-block.sh) and its property tests, not from a hash of the output.
resources.notes: core.hooksPath is set --local to an ABSOLUTE path on this machine (measured 2026-08-02: /Users/tank/code/crypto-quant-signal-mcp/.git/hooks), so every worktree resolves to this one file regardless of $GIT_COMMON_DIR. That makes the blast radius worse, not better, and CLAUDE.md's 'no custom core.hooksPath' claim is false.

resources.invariant: Same composability contract as pre-push. Until OPS-SHARED-WORKTREE-STATE-REGISTRY-W1 this hook was a whole-file `exec` that truncated anything already present; it is now a guarded block, so a second pre-commit consumer can be added without erasing the first.
resources._sha256_reason: Same as hook-pre-push — generated per install.

resources.invariant: The script must be reachable from the resolved remote default ref before the block may be installed (UNPUBLISHED_DEP). A worktree lacking it skips loudly with a ledger row rather than blocking the push.
resources._sha256_reason: Repo-tracked; git is the integrity mechanism.

resources.invariant: Same publish precondition as every block. THIS IS THE ONE WITH REAL RESIDUAL EXPOSURE when skipped.
resources._backstopped_by_reason: NOT backstopped, and cannot be. The gate reasons about the set of live worktrees; a CI runner is a fresh clone with exactly one, so deploy.yml runs only its --self-test (deploy.yml:269). A worktree lacking this file therefore has NO stale_base protection at all — measured 2026-08-02 at 55 of 74 checkouts. Reported separately from the backstopped gates because one undifferentiated 'unguarded' count would be true and useless.
resources._sha256_reason: Repo-tracked; git is the integrity mechanism.

resources.invariant: Same publish precondition. This is the block whose 2026-08-01 install — for a script present in one worktree only — deadlocked every parallel session and motivated this registry.
resources._sha256_reason: Repo-tracked; git is the integrity mechanism.

resources.invariant: Same publish precondition. Present in 74/74 checkouts as measured — the only gate with full coverage, because the script predates every live worktree.
resources._backstopped_by_reason: Local-only by design (it inspects the staged diff), but unlike session-drift its coverage is complete, so the absence of a CI backstop costs nothing today.
resources._sha256_reason: Repo-tracked; git is the integrity mechanism.

resources.invariant: Refuses HISTORY DESTRUCTION — a non-fast-forward or a deletion — on a ref declared in ops/push-safety-config.json, and NOTHING else. Ordinary fast-forward pushes, brand-new branches and every non-protected ref are explicitly allowed: this repo's LAW is auto-commit + auto-push and merges land as fast-forwards, so a conventional main-protection hook would halt every wave. Converts two CLAUDE.md laws ('Never force push to main/master', 'Never reset --hard / push --force / branch -D without auth') from prose into mechanical enforcement — measured 2026-08-02, ZERO of the four then-live blocks read the hook's stdin, so neither law was enforced by anything.
resources._backstopped_by_reason: CI runs --self-test ONLY. The live check needs a real push's stdin, which a CI runner does not have — the same structural limit that keeps check-session-drift.mjs and check-shared-state.mjs self-test-only. tests/unit/push-safety.test.ts covers the same logic a second way, deliberately: a dedicated workflow step keeps CI coverage if that test is ever quarantined.
resources._sha256_reason: Repo-tracked; git is the integrity mechanism.
resources.notes: Sorts FIRST under the helper's canonical LC_ALL=C block order (push-safety < session-drift < shared-state < source-greppable < test-gate) — the cheapest guard and the most consequential, so history destruction is refused in milliseconds rather than after a full vitest run. CONSEQUENCE: it CONSUMES the hook's stdin. Measured, none of the other four read stdin, so nothing breaks today; a future stdin-reading block would find it drained and should tee here rather than reorder. This was the FIRST consumer of scripts/lib/hook-block.sh written by someone other than its author, and it installed with no --allow-unpublished: the three-state publish precondition correctly reported 'pending merge' and allowed it.

resources.invariant: This reconciler polices the shared hooks, and is itself installed by the mechanism it polices (scripts/lib/hook-block.sh) — deliberate dogfooding: a guard exempt from its own contract is the first one to rot.
resources._backstopped_by_reason: CI runs --self-test ONLY. A live --check on a CI runner is structurally vacuous — one worktree, no installed hooks — so it would pass over an empty corpus and read as coverage. Same treatment deploy.yml:269 already gives check-session-drift.mjs.
resources._sha256_reason: Repo-tracked; git is the integrity mechanism.

resources.invariant: ONE SQLite file, in WAL mode, shared by every worktree's test run. src/lib/performance-db.ts:36 resolves `process.env.PERFORMANCE_DB_PATH || ~/.crypto-quant-signal/performance.db`, so PERFORMANCE_DB_PATH is the isolation lever and it already exists — no new mechanism is needed, only a declared contract. Measured 2026-08-02: 30,638,080 bytes with live -shm/-wal siblings.
resources._sha256_reason: A live database mutated by every test run; a hash is meaningless.

exempt_consumers.reason: OPS-ANALYTICS-EXT-PARALLEL-FLAKE-W1 measured 5/5 failures with a concurrent writer versus 1/15 serial, because it asserts pre/post deltas on WHOLE-TABLE aggregates while other processes INSERT into request_log. It was the FIRST suite to set PERFORMANCE_DB_PATH; it is no longer the only one — see the four rows below.

OPS-PARALLEL-SESSION-CAPACITY-W2 Ch3. Asserts by_source is an empty array over a WHOLE WINDOW, keyed on neither source nor session, so ANY foreign mcp_connect row breaks it — a disjoint sentinel prefix cannot help, and that window is already collided in-run by funnel-snapshot.test.ts. This is the file W1 caught failing on 2 of 5 concurrent gate runs with a genuine assertion mismatch.

OPS-PARALLEL-SESSION-CAPACITY-W2 Ch3. Asserts prefix-BLIND absolute aggregates (quota_hit soft/hard/block = 3/2/1, identity_coverage 2/1/1/0.5, mcp_tools_list = 3). Isolating it is what forced the deploy.yml cold-DB pre-warm to be re-pointed in the same commit: a pre-warm aimed at an isolated suite warms a temp dir and warms nothing.
OPS-PARALLEL-SESSION-CAPACITY-W2 Ch3. Same class: absolute candidate counts over request_log / quota_usage that any concurrent writer perturbs.
OPS-PARALLEL-SESSION-CAPACITY-W2 Ch3. Same class: column-ensure + backfill assertions over shared tables.

resources.notes: Every other suite that touches the DB writes the developer's real file. vitest.config.ts sets no global PERFORMANCE_DB_PATH (verified). That is the declared contract, not an accident: CONCURRENT_WRITER reports it rather than blocking, because forcing isolation on every suite is a separate wave with its own blast radius. OPS-PARALLEL-SESSION-CAPACITY-W2 Ch3 isolated the four suites whose assertions are prefix-BLIND (measured: 3 concurrent processes against the shared DB failed 1-8 tests EACH in every round; with isolation, 0) and deliberately left the rest, since a suite scoped to its own uniquely-named rows is not exposed. STILL OPEN and NOT closed by isolation: the concurrent cold-open MIGRATION race at src/lib/performance-db.ts:400-411 (bare ALTER, no IF NOT EXISTS, no lock, no busy_timeout) — the Postgres twin at :430-435 already carries the defense and a comment naming the race, so the SQLite gap is a known, undefended asymmetry. Owner: OPS-SQLITE-COLD-OPEN-MIGRATION-RACE-W{NEXT}.

resources.invariant: TSV: timestamp, event (SKIP | UNPUBLISHED_OVERRIDE), block name, worktree, script. A deliberate fail-open must be loud AND auditable — this file is the audit half, and SKIP_LEDGER_STALE is what turns it into an escalation rather than a log nobody reads.

Records UNGATED PUSHES only — a blocked run let nothing through, so it is not a ledger event. The next GREEN run reports and clears it. Registered here so the hook-skip ledger is recognisably the SAME convention rather than a second dialect; measured 0 bytes on 2026-08-02, i.e. never yet written.

Deploys a RESOLVED COMMIT, never a working directory, and refuses a ref that is not an ancestor of origin/main. It is cross-repo by construction (takes --repo), which is why it lives here and in neither consumer repo. This SUPERSEDES the ops/deploy/assert-deploy-ref.sh that this wave's spec proposed: never deploying a working tree dominates asserting on one, so a second primitive was deliberately NOT built.
resources._sha256_reason: The canonical sha256 lives on the monitoring-inventory row and is reconciled daily. A second recorded hash is a second thing that can drift — the exact law the monitoring-inventory arc codified.
resources.notes: Rollout to the remaining services is OPS-HOST-DEPLOY-PROVENANCE-ROLLOUT-W{NEXT} (measured: of 16 /opt dirs, 10 are not git checkouts and NONE records a deployed SHA). Deliberately not pre-empted here.

resources.invariant: Daily L2 detect: compares the live /opt/algovault-bot tree against DEPLOYED_MANIFEST.sha256, written FROM THE COMMIT by host-deploy.sh. Registered here because it is the detection half of the incident-B pair whose L1 half is host-deploy-primitive; the two must be retired together or not at all.
resources._sha256_reason: Canonical sha256 + installed_at + schedule already live on the monitoring-inventory row (id `bot-deploy-parity`, schedule `37 6 * * *`, install_state `installed`). Cross-referenced, never duplicated.

worktree_roots._doc: OPS-WORKTREE-ROOT-CONFINEMENT-W2 CH2. Worktree placement was the last emergent shared resource on this machine: it is CWD-derived and tool-version-dependent (three placements measured inside one 24h window), so it cannot be documented, only DECLARED. Paths are ABSOLUTE — a tilde row matches nothing resolved from `git worktree list --porcelain`, i.e. an exemption that silently does not exist.

repo_root.reason: the ONE repo root; a second root is the duplicate-clone generator (2 live duplicates prove it)

worktree_roots.destination_reason: dot-prefixed so ~/code reads as a plain list of repos; outside every repo tree so the vitest-discovery pathology (1779 discovered test files vs 298 real) is structurally impossible rather than merely detected; promotes the convention 4 worktrees already follow
worktree_roots.payload_floor_reason: 1 MB — 256x above observed noise (a 4 KB .env.local, copied into every worktree by cc-session.sh by design; resolve with `grep -n '.env.local' scripts/cc-session.sh`); 15x below the smallest real payload (15.5 MB). The margin above noise is comfortable; 15x below the smallest payload is tighter than it looks, so anything landing in the band floor -> 15.5 MB REPORTS for human classification rather than passing silently.

payload_report_band_kb.reason: floor -> smallest known real payload (15.5 MB). A worktree in this gap is neither noise nor a known dataset: report it, never auto-classify.

R1_confinement.baseline_note: 35 as check-worktree-root.mjs measures it, 2026-08-09: NON-EXEMPT worktrees outside worktree_root. This is the guard's OWN metric — CH1's raw 40 counted exempt paths too, and a baseline that is not the number the promotion criterion reads is a baseline nobody can compare against. A PREFIX predicate, not a shape predicate: the 4 compliant worktrees are direct children of worktree_root, and an exact <repo>/<task> rule would score them violations too. The population moves (43->48 worktrees during CH2 alone), so this is history, not an expectation — promotion reads max_violations, never this figure.

promotion.reason: count AND date: a criterion with no time bound can never fire if the population does not heal on its own

R2_nesting.predicate: no worktree path inside any primary's or any other worktree's tree
R2_nesting.baseline_note: 10 as the guard measures it, 2026-08-09: non-exempt worktrees inside a primary's or another worktree's tree. All 10 sit in crypto-quant-signal-mcp/.claude/worktrees/. Two of them were generated by the tool WHILE this fix was being planned. R2 is NOT a subset of R1: those paths are under ~/code yet nested.

promotion.reason: separate date from R1: R2 reaches zero in CH4/CH6 and must not be held hostage to R1's longer tail

R3_shape.baseline_note: 38 non-exempt worktrees do not match <worktree_root>/<repo>/<task>. Reported, never gated; CH6 drives it to zero.
